name: El Quemao
notes: Heavy, hollow left (and shorter right) over shallow volcanic reef in front of La Santa village; entry from the pier.

name: La Santa Left
notes: Long, hollow left over lava reef in La Santa bay; works most of the year.

name: La Santa Centro
notes: Mellower, longer reef wave between the La Santa left and right.

name: La Santa Right
notes: Powerful right over lava reef that holds big swells.

name: Caleta de Caballo
notes: Rights and a left over reef either side of a narrow gap in the coastal rocks.

name: San Juan
notes: Long, fast left over reef west of Caleta de Famara; contest venue.

name: El Muelle (Caleta de Famara)
notes: Fast lefts and rights over rock by the Caleta de Famara pier.

name: El Cagao
notes: Short, fast reef peak at Caleta de Famara.

name: Playa de Famara
notes: Long sandy beach under the Famara cliffs with peaks for every level; main surf-school beach.

name: Playa de La Cantería
notes: Exposed beach near Órzola with an easier inside and a faster left off the rocks on the rising tide.

name: Jameos del Agua
notes: Long left over reef on the north-east coast, also a down-the-line wave spot for windsurfers.

name: Playa de La Garita (Arrieta)
notes: Dark-sand beach at Arrieta with short peaks; windsurf option in northerly wind.

name: Las Cucharas
notes: Main windsurf bay of Costa Teguise: flat water inside, reef waves outside in NE trades.

name: Los Charcos
notes: Small lagoon and reef wave at Costa Teguise used when the wind is too northerly for Las Cucharas.

name: Playa Honda
notes: Long beach south of Arrecife used as a flat-water alternative when Las Cucharas is too windy.

name: Playa Francesa (La Graciosa)
notes: Long right on La Graciosa's south shore.

name: Montaña Amarilla (La Graciosa)
notes: Fast left at the south-west tip of La Graciosa.

name: La Baja del Ganado (La Graciosa)
notes: Short, explosive right-hand tube over volcanic reef near Las Conchas.

name: El Cotillo
notes: Long west-facing beach south of El Cotillo; mellow on small days, heavy close-outs in big swell.

name: Cotillo Lagos
notes: Sheltered lagoons north of El Cotillo with flat water for learners.

name: Playa de Esquinzo
notes: Cliff-backed beach break south of El Cotillo, reached by track.

name: Playa del Águila (La Escalera)
notes: Beach break below a steep stairway on the north-west coast.

name: Punta Gorda
notes: Right over a low volcanic shelf on the north-west corner.

name: Punta Blanca
notes: North Shore reef with a long paddle to a wide take-off zone.

name: Derecha de los Alemanes
notes: Fast, hollow right over shallow volcanic reef at El Hierro on the North Shore.

name: Izquierda del Hierro
notes: A-frame left with a long shoulder at El Hierro, best in winter groundswell.

name: Majanicho
notes: Peeling right over reef in the bay of the Majanicho fishing hamlet; shallow at low tide.

name: Mejillones
notes: Exposed North Shore reef reached by gravel track.

name: Generosa
notes: Left over lava reef with a rocky entry and no beach.

name: Bristol (Shooting Gallery)
notes: Steep, fast reef peak west of Corralejo, shallow at low tide.

name: El Muelle (Harbour Wall)
notes: Left over reef next to the old Corralejo harbour wall.

name: Rocky Point Inside
notes: Reef just south of Waikiki in Corralejo bay; best at high tide.

name: Lobos
notes: Long, powerful right on Isla de Lobos, reached by boat from Corralejo.

name: Flag Beach
notes: Main kite and windsurf beach south of Corralejo with a reef ramp offshore.

name: El Burro (Glass Beach)
notes: Reef peaks off the Corralejo dunes; kite and windsurf in NW wind.

name: La Pared
notes: Consistent west-coast beach break with rocks and strong rips on the south side.

name: Playa de Garcey
notes: Remote beach by the American Star wreck with strong currents.

name: Cofete
notes: Wild, remote beach on Jandía's windward side; no lifeguards and dangerous currents.

name: Punta del Tigre (La Turbia)
notes: Isolated right-hand reef near the Jandía lighthouse road.

name: Matas Blancas
notes: Flat-water speed spot north of Costa Calma with offshore trade wind.

name: Sotavento (Playa de la Barca)
notes: Very windy beach and tidal lagoon; long-running windsurf World Cup venue.

name: El Confital
notes: Hollow right on a shallow shelf at La Isleta; works best at high tide.

name: La Barra (Las Canteras)
notes: Natural reef bar in front of Las Canteras with short, playful waves.

name: La Cícer
notes: Sandy southern end of Las Canteras; the island's main learner spot.

name: Los Muellitos
notes: Left by the jetty at the south end of Las Canteras.

name: El Lloret
notes: Long right point over rock west of the Muellitos jetty.

name: El Pico de La Laja
notes: Hollow left over shallow volcanic reef at the north end of La Laja beach.

name: Quintanilla
notes: Fast left over rock that picks up the most swell on the north coast.

name: Boquines
notes: Right point and fast left over reef beside the El Altillo pools.

name: Soledad (El Paso)
notes: Fickle, powerful wave in Moya that only breaks a few times per season.

name: El Circo (San Felipe)
notes: Short, hollow left and right at San Felipe.

name: El Frontón
notes: Heavy bodyboard slab over shallow reef near Gáldar; world-tour bodyboard venue.

name: Jinámar
notes: Pebble-and-sand kite spot used when the wind is too northerly for Vargas.

name: Vargas
notes: Stony beach with strong trade wind and waves; kite zone at the south end.

name: Pozo Izquierdo
notes: World-class wave-sailing spot with very strong summer trade wind; World Cup venue.

name: Mosca Point
notes: Long left point next to Pozo that needs a big swell.

name: Faro de Maspalomas
notes: Right point over reef in front of the lighthouse, best with south or west swell.

name: Arguineguín
notes: Long right point on the south coast that needs a big south or west swell.

name: Almáciga
notes: Sand-and-cobble beach in Anaga with lefts and rights; gets rippy when big.

name: Igueste de San Andrés
notes: Left that only breaks with north-east swell wrapping into the Anaga bay.

name: El Roquete (Punta del Hidalgo)
notes: Powerful left over boulders at the point of Punta del Hidalgo.

name: El Lobo (Bajamar)
notes: Long left over pebbles and reef in front of Bajamar.

name: El Socorro (Los Realejos)
notes: Popular north-coast beach with a right point at the west end and an A-frame in the middle.

name: Punta Blanca (Alcalá)
notes: Left (and short right) over volcanic reef at Guía de Isora; contest venue.

name: La Caleta (Adeje)
notes: Reef right near La Caleta village that works with summer south swell.

name: La Izquierda (Las Palmeras)
notes: Tubing left over volcanic reef at Playa de las Américas, best in winter north-west swell.

name: El Medio
notes: Gentle, flat-reef bay in the middle of Playa de las Américas.

name: La Fitenia
notes: Reef beside the Los Cristianos harbour wall that needs south swell.

name: La Machacona
notes: Powerful left tube close to shore near La Tejita in summer south swell.

name: El Médano
notes: Windy bay with flat water to the south and the island's main kite and windsurf schools.

name: El Cabezo
notes: Wave-sailing reef next to El Médano with diagonal onshore trade wind.

name: Playa de Nogales
notes: Cliff-backed black-sand beach in Puntallana; strong currents.
